text:
alex: Morning handoff — quick summary of overnight. We had a flurry of KV-cache eviction spikes in eu-west around 03:12 UTC that caused graceful fallbacks to smaller model variants and generated ~120 503-ish responses to a small set of customers. Incident bot paged. No SLO breach yet but elevated error rate for ~13 minutes.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20260032 — KV cache thrash -> model fallback. PagerDuty alert: P12345.

alex: What we did last night:
- rotated eviction thresholds (temporary raise)
- enabled model-variant fallback policy to use gpt-small for tail requests
- kicked a rolling restart on nodepool-eu-kv-2 (graceful)
- added a short-term routing rule to prefer eu-central as failover

jamie: Thanks Alex. Customer impact assessment: affected 7 orgs, top 2 saw ~1.4% request failures during window, others negligible. Outreach: support already sent proactive note to the top 2.

sara: Logs show a spike in small seq lengths causing cache churn — looks like a traffic pattern change from a partner integration that started running headless scraping on a short interval. I opened a ticket with them.

mike: Re: roll restart — noticed one pod restarted slower due to kube-probe flapping (readiness race). Filed ENGOPS-884. For now, healthcheck probe backoff adjusted to 20s.

lee: Primary/secondary for today: I can take primary til 14:00 UTC, mike will be secondary. After 14:00 Jamie takes primary, Sara secondary. There is a coverage gap 05:00–06:30 UTC (Europe early morning) where we're light on on-call overlap — assigning floater to watch alerts.

alex: Next steps for oncoming shift:
- primary: monitor INC-20260032 runbook steps 1–4 (cache thresholds, routing, pod restarts). Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-eviction-thrash
- verify error rate trending down to baseline (<0.2%) for 30m window
- don't roll new model or infra changes until cleanup is green
- if errors spike again, escalate to eng-runtime and open a hotfix branch

jamie: Quick commands to check live metrics:
```
# check 5m error rate eu-west
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/api/query?m=error_rate.euwest&window=5m" | jq .
# check KV eviction count
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=kvcache --tail=200 | grep -i eviction | tail -n 50
```

sara: Also watch for repeated small requests from the partner. If we see >1000/min from a single client, block at the gateway and add to the partner ticket.

oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window later today 22:00 UTC for infra patching — won't affect this incident but heads-up.

mike: Action item list (short):
- [ ] validate partner rate-limiting rule (mike) — ETA 1h
- [ ] follow up with partner integration (sara) — ETA 3h
- [ ] revert eviction threshold to normal after 2h stable (alex) — manual check
- [ ] update incident doc with customer outreach notes (jamie) — in progress

lee: If the new floater isn't on in the coverage gap, ping #general and @oncall-floater. Also tagging @pagerduty-bot to ensure escalation policy is healthy.

pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy P-High active for P12345. Next rotate in 12m.

alex: Wrapping up: status = monitoring, mitigation applied, customer outreach underway. Primary/secondary for next 12h: lee primary -> mike secondary until 14:00 UTC; then jamie primary -> sara secondary. Leave a note in the incident doc on any config changes.

jamie: thumbs up. I'll take over the bridge at 14:00 UTC. If anyone sees a new page before handoff, call my cell.

sara: adding runbook pointer inline:
Runbook excerpt:
```
1) Increase eviction threshold: kubectl patch configmap kv-config -p '{"data":{"eviction_pct":"0.85"}}'
2) Enable fallback policy: rwdctl models fallback enable --region eu-west --variant gpt-small
3) Add routing rule: rwdctl route add --from eu-west --to eu-central --weight 0.2
4) Monitor errors: sla_monitor watch INC-20260032 --window 30m
```

mike: I'll validate the probe backoff change and follow up in ENGOPS-884.

alex: Thanks all — handoff complete.
